body:
Can you try running Godot with [validation layers](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/engine_details/development/debugging/vulkan/vulkan_validation_layers.html) enabled? If there's a deadlock occurring, I believe it should be caught based on that [function's valid usage](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkAcquireNextImageKHR.html).

Additionally, if you use the compatibility renderer (aka OpenGL), does the issue go away? (`--rendering-driver opengl3`)

@rsubtil I will try this, thanks. What's odd is that I can't reproduce this on another Arch Linux (Wayland with KDE) system with an Intel CPU and Nvidia GPU:

```
Godot v4.6.1.stable (14d19694e) - Arch Linux #1 ZEN SMP PREEMPT Sat, 01 Jun 2024 22:17:18 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce 830M (nvidia; 580.126.09) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-5500U CPU @ 2.40GHz (4 threads) - 13.66 GiB memory
```

Maybe this is related to AMD GPU?

I have tested again after installing Vulkan validation layers on my AMD GPU system.
```
❯ sudo pacman -S vulkan-validation-layers
[...]
Packages (1) vulkan-validation-layers-1.4.341.0-2
```

<details><summary>I have used the `--gpu-validate` and `--gpu-abort` commandline arguments and got to the same point as before - the game froze on a loading screen (did not crash) until I killed the process. I see some Vulkan errors, but I don't see a culprit here. (click the arrow to expand and read the entire log - it's long)
</summary>
